answer: Cross-Epoch Citation Drift Rule. Each identity’s citations to peers are scored per epoch; enforcement compares consecutive score vectors and flags identities whose drift exceeds a tight threshold, forcing persistence across the tundra of inactive periods. A sybil must sustain consistent citation patterns through every gale of reweighting, not just spike once. On the horizon, each maintained identity costs continuous genuine interactions per epoch; scaling to N identities multiplies that labor by N, making forgery linear-cost, not free.
